## `addGroupIndices`: Add group indices to a data frame



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Adds an integer column identifying the group to which each row belongs.
Groups are defined by one or more columns and follow the grouping behavior of
[dplyr::group_by()].
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>addGroupIndices(dfr, ...)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="addGroupIndices_+3A_dfr">dfr</code></td>
<td>
<p>A data frame containing the grouping columns.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="addGroupIndices_+3A_...">...</code></td>
<td>
<p>Unquoted columns in 'dfr' that define the groups. These arguments
are passed to [dplyr::group_by()].</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>'dfr' with its rows and existing columns preserved and an integer
'.gid' column appended. Rows with the same values of the grouping columns
receive the same group index. An existing '.gid' column is replaced.
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>y &lt;- as.character(11:20)
s &lt;- as.character(1:3)
x &lt;- as.character(1:2)
z &lt;- seq(25, 50, 5)
dfr &lt;- tidyr::expand_grid(y, s, x, z)

dfrp &lt;- addGroupIndices(dfr, y, s, x)
head(dfrp)
dplyr::count(dfrp, y, s, x, .gid)

</code></pre>

## `advance_pop_one_season`: Advance population component one season step



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>This function will advance the population component one seasonal step
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>advance_pop_one_season(
  n_i,
  p,
  doInstProcesses1st,
  doGrowth,
  doSSB_BeforeGrowth
)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="advance_pop_one_season_+3A_n_i">n_i</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> abundance vector by population class
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="advance_pop_one_season_+3A_p">p</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> list of population processes to apply
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="advance_pop_one_season_+3A_doInstProcesses1st">doInstProcesses1st</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> flag to do instantaneous processes (i.e., growth) first (TRUE/FALSE)
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="advance_pop_one_season_+3A_doGrowth">doGrowth</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> flag to evaluate growth (TRUE/FALSE)
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="advance_pop_one_season_+3A_doSSB_BeforeGrowth">doSSB_BeforeGrowth</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> flag to do spawning stock abundance calculation before growth (TRUE) or after (FALSE)
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>The returned list has elements
</p>

<ul>
<li><p> n_f - final population abundance vector
</p>
</li>
<li><p> n_ss - spawning stock abundance
</p>
</li>
<li><p> c_fn - total catch abundance by fleet (not necessarily mortality)
</p>
</li>
<li><p> rm_n - retained catch mortality (abundance) by fleet
</p>
</li>
<li><p> dm_fn - discard catch mortality (abundance) by fleet
</p>
</li></ul>



<h3>Value</h3>

<p>list including population abundance at end of time step (see Details)
</p>

## `createAggregationMatrix`: Create a sparse aggregation matrix



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Creates a sparse matrix that maps rows of a data frame to groups defined by
one or more columns. Multiplying the matrix by a vector with one value per
input row calculates sums for each group.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>createAggregationMatrix(dfr, ...)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="createAggregationMatrix_+3A_dfr">dfr</code></td>
<td>
<p>A data frame containing the grouping columns.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="createAggregationMatrix_+3A_...">...</code></td>
<td>
<p>Unquoted columns in 'dfr' that define the groups. These arguments
are passed to [dplyr::group_by()].</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>A named list with two elements:
</p>

<dl>
<dt>'aggM'</dt><dd><p>A sparse matrix with one row per group and one column per
row of 'dfr'.</p>
</dd>
<dt>'aggTbl'</dt><dd><p>A data frame containing the unique grouping combinations,
in the same order as the rows of 'aggM'.</p>
</dd>
</dl>



<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>y &lt;- as.character(11:20)
s &lt;- as.character(1:3)
x &lt;- as.character(1:2)
z &lt;- seq(25, 50, 5)
dfr &lt;- tidyr::expand_grid(y, s, x, z)

lst &lt;- createAggregationMatrix(dfr, y, s, x)
values &lt;- as.matrix(dfr["z"])
group_sums &lt;- lst$aggM %*% values

lst$aggTbl |&gt; dplyr::mutate(sum=as.vector(group_sums));

</code></pre>

## `evalTextAsCode`: Evaluate text as lines of code



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Function to evaluate text as lines of code.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>evalTextAsCode(strv, frame = 0)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="evalTextAsCode_+3A_strv">strv</code></td>
<td>
<p>- character vector with lines of code to evaluate.</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>The lines of 'code' in strv are evaluated in the frame specified by
'frame'. If 'frame' is non-negative, it specifies the parent frame relative to the
caller (so &lsquo;frame=0', the deault, is evaluated in the caller&rsquo;s frame). If 'frame' is negative,
the lines of code are evaluated in the environment specified by its absolute value.
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>nothing
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>
str = "
  v1  = 5;
  v2 = 1:v1;
  sum = list(x="contr.sum",m="contr.sum");
      ";
# example code

</code></pre>


<!-- Source: man/evalTextAsDataframe.Rd -->
## `evalTextAsDataframe`: Evaluate a character vector as a dataframe (a <code>tbl_df</code>)



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Function to evaluate a character vector as a dataframe (a <code>tbl_df</code>).
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>evalTextAsDataframe(char_vec, comment = "#")
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="evalTextAsDataframe_+3A_char_vec">char_vec</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> character vector to parse/evaluate as a dataframe
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="evalTextAsDataframe_+3A_comment">comment</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> string indicating that what follows is a comment
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>Each element in <code>char_vec</code> is regarded as a line of text (as in a text file).
The dataframe structure and column types are determined by <code>readr::read_table()</code>.
</p>
<p>This function differs from <code>extractDataframe()</code> in that, after comments are removed are
removed from the input character vector <code>char_vec</code>, the resulting
character vector is regarded as defining the dataframe. In <code>extractDataframe()</code>,
the input character vector may be a much larger section of text than what defines the
dataframe to be extracted, but the number of rows (<code>n</code>) to extract is known as, is the index of
the element to begin with (<code>start</code>).
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>a dataframe (actually a <code>tbl_df</code>, see <code>tibble::tibble()</code>)
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>
# example code
str&lt;-paste0('
  id        function  frame   params              description
  pwrLaw1   pwrLaw1   mfALL   pA,pB               w(z)_=_pA_*_(z^pB)
  pwrLaw2   pwrLaw2   mf2024  pLnA,pLnS,pB,pZ0    w(z)_=_exp(pLnA+pLnS+pB*ln(z/pZ0))
')
dfr = txt |&gt; splitText() |&gt; evalTextAsDataframe();

</code></pre>

## `evalTextAsDigits`: Evaluate strings in a character vector as digits



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Function to evaluate strings in a character vector as digits.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>evalTextAsDigits(x)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="evalTextAsDigits_+3A_x">x</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> character vector to parse/evaluate
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>For each element in <code>x</code>, everything except for digits is removed and
the resulting character value is converted to an integer.
</p>

</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>evalTextAsDigits(c("ab23","cd42","a42 b23"))

</code></pre>


<!-- Source: man/evalTextAsList.Rd -->
## `evalTextAsList`: Evaluate a list from a character vector



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Function to evaluate a list from a character vector.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>evalTextAsList(strv, split = "&lt;-", verbose = FALSE)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="evalTextAsList_+3A_strv">strv</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> character vector to parse/evaluate
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="evalTextAsList_+3A_split">split</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> character(s) to use to split lines into name and value (default=&quot;&lt;-&quot;)
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="evalTextAsList_+3A_verbose">verbose</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> flag to print diagnostic info
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>Each quantity assigned using <code style="white-space: pre;">&#8288;&lt;-&#8288;</code> in <code>strv</code> is interpreted as an equation defining an element of the returned list.
Quantities assigned using <code>=</code> outside a list structure are evaluated locally for use in constructing a list element of
the returned list. Attributes for a list element of the returned list must be assigned (see example code 2) immediately after
the list element.
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>list with named elements
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>
# example code 1
str=paste(
  'MODEL_DIMS
  y &lt;- 2020:2024;                           #--years
  s &lt;- 1;                                   #--seasons
  r &lt;- "EBS";                               #--regions
  x &lt;- c("male","female");                  #--sex classes
  m &lt;- c("immature","mature");              #--maturity state classes
  p &lt;- c("new_shell","old_shell");          #--post-molt ages
  zc &lt;- seq(55.5,104.5,5);                  #--size bin cutpoints
  f &lt;- c("TCF","SCF","NMFS");               #--fleets
  END');
strv = str |&gt; splitText() |&gt; extractLines("MODEL_DIMS","END");
lstDims = evalTextAsList(strv);
# example code 2
  str=paste(
  'MODEL_DIMS
    r &lt;- "EBS";
    miz = as.character(seq(25,75,5)); #--size bin midpoints for immature males
    mmz = as.character(seq(50,75,5)); #--size bin midpoints for mature males
    fiz = as.character(seq(25,65,5)); #--size bin midpoints for immature females
    fmz = as.character(seq(30,65,5)); #--size bin midpoints for mature females
    x&lt;-list(male=list(imm=list(`new`=miz,
                                 `old`=miz),
                        mat=list(`new`=mmz,
                                 `old`=mmz,
                                 `very`=mmz)
                      ),
              female=list(imm=list(`new`=fiz,
                                   `old`=fiz),
                          mat=list(`new`=fmz,
                                   `old`=fmz)
                         )
             );
    attr(x,"dmnms") = c("x","m","p","z");#--define order of dimensions in nested list
  END'
  )
  strv = str |&gt; splitText() |&gt; extractLines("MODEL_DIMS","END");
  lstDms = evalTextAsList(strv);

</code></pre>

## `extractDataframe`: Extract a dataframe (a <code>tibble::tibble()</code>) from a character vector



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Function to a dataframe (a <code>tibble::tibble()</code>) from a character vector.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>extractDataframe(txt, n, start, comment = "#")
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="extractDataframe_+3A_txt">txt</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> character vector to search
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="extractDataframe_+3A_n">n</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> number of non-comment lines to extract
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="extractDataframe_+3A_start">start</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> index into <code>txt</code> to regard as the start of the search
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="extractDataframe_+3A_comment">comment</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> character indicating the following text in the string is a comment
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>Each element in <code>txt</code> is regarded as a line of text (as in a text file).
The dataframe structure and column types are determined by <code>readr::read_table()</code>.
</p>

<ul>
<li><p>txt - character vector of length <code>n</code> with comment lines removed (i.e., a subset of <code>txt</code>)
</p>
</li>
<li><p>end - index of the last element extracted in the input <code>txt</code> vector
</p>
</li></ul>

<p>This function differs from <code>evalTextAsDataframe()</code> in that
the input character vector may be a much larger section of text than what defines the
dataframe to be extracted, but the number of rows (<code>n</code>) to extract is known, as is the index of
the element to begin with (<code>start</code>). In <code>evalTextAsDataframe()</code>, after comments are removed are
removed from the input character vector <code>char_vec</code>, the resulting
character vector is regarded as defining the dataframe.
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>list with elements <code>txt</code> and <code>end</code> (see details)
</p>

<!-- Source: man/extractNumericValue.Rd -->
## `extractNumericValue`: Extract a numeric value from a line of text



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Function to extract a numeric value from a line of text.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>extractNumericValue(txt, comment = "#")
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="extractNumericValue_+3A_txt">txt</code></td>
<td>
<p>- input text string (1-element character vector)</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="extractNumericValue_+3A_comment">comment</code></td>
<td>
<p>- string used to split text into value and comments (default=&quot;#&quot;)</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>The 1-line input text is split into a character vector using [stringr::str_split_1()] and
the first element of the result is retained. Whitespace preceding and following the retained
text is also removed (but &quot;interior&quot; whitespace is retained). The result is converted to numeric
using [as.numeric()].
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>a 1-element numeric vector
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'># example code
txt = "  45.27  #--input value of interest";
extractNumericValue(txt)
txt = "'hows this'  #--input text of interest";
extractTextValue(txt);  #--returns NA

</code></pre>


<!-- Source: man/extractTextAfterString.Rd -->
## `extractTextAfterString`: Extract text after a string



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Function to extract text after a string
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>extractTextAfterString(txt, str)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="extractTextAfterString_+3A_txt">txt</code></td>
<td>
<p>- character vector from which to extract strings</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="extractTextAfterString_+3A_str">str</code></td>
<td>
<p>- string to extract after (see NOTE under details)</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>For each element in the vector, this extracts the string following
the 'after' string from each element of the input
character vector, or 'NA' if no 'after' string found.
</p>
<p>NOTE: Characters with special regex meanings (e.g., &quot;)&quot;,&quot;]&quot;) need to
be double-escaped to use in 'str'.
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>character vector of extracted strings
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'># example code
extractTextAfterString("test:fred[x,y]==0","==");
extractTextAfterString(c("fred[x,y]==0: FALSE","b[z0]: 1"),":");
extractTextAfterString("fred[x,y[z]]=0","=");
extractTextAfterString("fred[x,y[z]]=0","\\[");
extractTextAfterString("fred[x,y[z]]=0","fred\\[");

</code></pre>

## `extractTextBetweenBrackets`: Extract text between first and last brackets



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Function to extract text between first and last brackets
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>extractTextBetweenBrackets(txt)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="extractTextBetweenBrackets_+3A_txt">txt</code></td>
<td>
<p>- character vector from which to extract strings</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>For each element in the vector, this extracts the string between the
*first* &quot;\[&quot; and *last* &quot;\]&quot; from each element of the input
character vector, or 'NA' if no matching brackets.
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>character vector of extracted strings
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'># example code
extractTextBetweenBrackets("fred[x,y]=0");
extractTextBetweenParens(c("fred[x,y]=0","b[z0]"));
extractTextBetweenParens("fred[x,y[z]]=0");

</code></pre>


<!-- Source: man/extractTextBetweenParens.Rd -->
## `extractTextBetweenParens`: Extract text between first and last parentheses



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Function to extract text between first and last parentheses
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>extractTextBetweenParens(txt)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="extractTextBetweenParens_+3A_txt">txt</code></td>
<td>
<p>- character vector from which to extract strings</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>For each element in the vector, this extracts the string between the
*first* &quot;(&quot; and *last* &quot;)&quot; from each element of the input
character vector, or 'NA' if no matching parentheses.
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>character vector of extracted strings
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'># example code
extractTextBetweenParens("fred(x,y)=0");
extractTextBetweenParens(c("fred(x,y)=0","b(z0)"));
extractTextBetweenParens("fred(x,y(z))=0");

</code></pre>

## `extractTextSection`: Extract a text section with only non-comment lines from a character vector



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Function to extract a text section with only non-comment lines from a character vector.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>extractTextSection(txt, n = length(txt), start = 1, comment = "#")
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="extractTextSection_+3A_txt">txt</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> character vector to search
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="extractTextSection_+3A_n">n</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> number of non-comment lines to extract (default=length(txt))
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="extractTextSection_+3A_start">start</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> index into <code>txt</code> to regard as the start of the search (default=1)
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="extractTextSection_+3A_comment">comment</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> character indicating the following text in the string is a comment
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>Each element in <code>txt</code> is regarded as a line of text (as in a text file).
The function searches for the first <code>n</code> non-comment lines and extracts them as a new vector.
The returned list has elements
</p>

<ul>
<li><p>txt - character vector of length <code>n</code> with comment lines removed (i.e., a subset of <code>txt</code>)
</p>
</li>
<li><p>end - index of the last element extracted in the input <code>txt</code> vector
</p>
</li></ul>



<h3>Value</h3>

<p>list with elements <code>txt</code> and <code>end</code> (see details)
</p>


<!-- Source: man/extractTextValue.Rd -->
## `extractTextValue`: Extract a (character) value from a line of text



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Function to extract a (character) value from a line of text.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>extractTextValue(txt, comment = "#")
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="extractTextValue_+3A_txt">txt</code></td>
<td>
<p>- input text string (1-element character vector)</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="extractTextValue_+3A_comment">comment</code></td>
<td>
<p>- string used to split text into value and comments (default=&quot;#&quot;)</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>The 1-line input text is split into a character vector using [stringr::str_split_1()] and
the first element of the result is retained. Whitespace preceding and following the retained
text is also removed (but &quot;interior&quot; whitespace is retained).
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>a 1-element character vector
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'># example code
txt = "'hows this'  #--input text of interest";
extractTextValue(txt)

</code></pre>

</p>

<pre><code class='language-R'>logistic(x)
</code></pre>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="logistic_+3A_x">x</code></td>
<td>
<p>- numeric object</p>

## `logit`: Convert values to the logit scale



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Function to convert values to the logit scale.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>logit(x)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="logit_+3A_x">x</code></td>
<td>
<p>- numeric object</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>inverse of logistic function. Values of 'x' outside the
(0,1) range generate NaNs.
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>log(x/(1-x)), with same names and class as 'x'
</p>

## `removeCommentLines`: Remove strings starting with a comment character



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Function to remove strings starting with a comment character.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>removeCommentLines(strv, comment = "#")
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="removeCommentLines_+3A_strv">strv</code></td>
<td>
<p>- character vector to remove comment lines from</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="removeCommentLines_+3A_comment">comment</code></td>
<td>
<p>- character(s) to regard as indicating a comment</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>a character vector with elements that don't start with a comment character
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>txt = c("#this is a comment",
        "  #so is this,even thought the line starts with blank space",
        "this is not a comment",
        "this is not either, but the first is line 3.");
removeCommentLines(txt); #--should be \code{txt[3:4]}

</code></pre>

</p>

<pre><code class='language-R'>skipCommentLines(txt, start, comment = "#")
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="skipCommentLines_+3A_txt">txt</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> character vector to search
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="skipCommentLines_+3A_start">start</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> index into <code>txt</code> to regard as the start of the search
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="skipCommentLines_+3A_comment">comment</code></td>
<td>

<ul>
<li><p> character indicating the following text in the string is a comment
</p>
</li></ul>
</td></tr>
</table>

## `symlogistic`: Calculate a 0-symmetric logistic function between -1 and 1



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Function to calculate a logistic function centered on 0
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>symlogistic(x)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="symlogistic_+3A_x">x</code></td>
<td>
<p>- numeric vector at which to calculate the symmetric logistic function</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>This is the inverse to 'symlogit' (see examples)
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>a numeric vector with the same size and names (if any) as 'x'
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>
##--R context
x = seq(-5,5,0.1);
y = symlogistic(x);
head(y);
xp = symlogit(y) - x
##--RTMB context
x = RTMB::AD(seq(-5,5,0.1),force=TRUE);
y = symlogistic(x);
head(y)

</code></pre>

## `symlogit`: Calculate a 0-symmetric logit function



<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Function to calculate a logit function centered on 0
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>symlogit(x)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="symlogit_+3A_x">x</code></td>
<td>
<p>- numeric vector with values from -1.0 to 1.0 at which to calculate the symmetric logit function</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>This is the inverse to 'symlogistic' (see examples)
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>a numeric vector with the same size and names (if any) as 'x'
</p>


<h3>Examples</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>
##--R context
x = seq(-0.99,0.99,0.01);
y = symlogit(x);
head(y);
xp = symlogistic(y) - x
##--RTMB context
x = RTMB::AD(seq(-0.49,0.49,0.01),force=TRUE);
y = symlogit(x);
head(y)

</code></pre>
